reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Koos Grading of Vestibular Schwannoma

version.label: Koos et al. (1998), grades 1–4
version.detail: Extrameatal extension and relation to the brainstem on MRI.

intendedPopulation: Patients with vestibular schwannoma on MRI.

options.label: Grade 2: Small tumour protruding into the cerebellopontine angle; no contact with the brainstem
Grade 3: Tumour occupying the cerebellopontine cistern without brainstem displacement
Grade 4: Large tumour with brainstem and cranial nerve displacement

resultStates.label: Grade 2
resultStates.summary: Small tumour protruding into the cerebellopontine angle; no contact with the brainstem.

resultStates.label: Grade 3
resultStates.summary: Tumour occupying the cerebellopontine cistern without brainstem displacement.

resultStates.label: Grade 4
resultStates.summary: Large tumour with brainstem and cranial nerve displacement.

clinicalContext.text: Widely used in choosing between observation, radiosurgery and microsurgery for vestibular schwannoma.

clinicalInsights.text: Brainstem compression: correlate with hydrocephalus and cranial nerve function.

limitations.text: Describes extension, not volume or growth rate.

limitations: Boundaries between grades 2 and 3 vary between readers.

confounders.effect: May behave differently from solid tumours of similar grade.

guideSections.what: Four grades of vestibular schwannoma extension.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess intracanalicular versus cisternal extension and brainstem contact or displacement.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with growth, hearing and patient factors.

sources.citation: Koos WT, Day JD, Matula C, Levy DI. Neurotopographic considerations in the microsurgical treatment of small acoustic neurinomas. J Neurosurg. 1998;88(3):506-512.
